speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) how many individuals and how many organisations have been prosecuted in relation to the shipments of elephant ivory and pangolin scales seized at our border checkpoints in 2019; and (b) if there is none, whether an update on the investigations can be provided.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One, whether NParks is also following the money; so, not just follow where the products are coming from or going to, but really follow the money trail.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Only then, can we get to the kingpins rather than always catching the runners involved in the wildlife smuggling network.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The second clarification is whether we can follow the British and work with our banks and financial institutions so that we can track these suspicious transactions that are linked to the wildlife smuggling network and halt the transactions in the first place.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think only then can we effectively address and wipe out this trade.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I had mentioned, NParks is helping with the international investigations into these cases.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: What about the second part of the question, so that we can be more pre-emptive?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We can get our banks and financial institutions to track all these suspicious transactions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Somebody paid for the shipments to be sent through Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can we audit and go to the money trail and find out who actually has been paying?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And then, finally, we can get the kingpin.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Otherwise, we are always arresting the runners who are already the low-level criminals.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Let us go high up the food chain.
